domains.proposed_domain: Conformal analysis and homogeneous Sobolev pullback

evidence.quote:
The Koebe function $f(z)=z/(1-z)^2$ belongs to $\mathcal S$ and satisfies $$\int_{\mathbb D}|f'|^{-2}\,dA=\infty,
 \qquad
 \int_{\mathbb D}|f'|^{2/3}\,dA=\infty.$$ Its inverse therefore fails area integrability at both $s=4$ and $s=4/3$.

exclusions.reason: The Koebe example gives divergence at both endpoints of the open range.

hypotheses.statement:
The Koebe function $f(z)=z/(1-z)^2$ belongs to $\mathcal S$ and satisfies $$\int_{\mathbb D}|f'|^{-2}\,dA=\infty,
 \qquad
 \int_{\mathbb D}|f'|^{2/3}\,dA=\infty.$$ Its inverse therefore fails area integrability at both $s=4$ and $s=4/3$.

If $f(z)=z+a_2z^2+\cdots$ belongs to $\mathcal S$, then $|a_2|\le2$ and, for $|z|=r<1$, $$\frac{1-r}{(1+r)^3}\le |f'(z)|\le\frac{1+r}{(1-r)^3},
 \qquad \frac r4\le |f(z)|\le\frac{r}{(1-r)^2}.
 \label{prelim:disk-bounds}$$ Every univalent holomorphic map $g$ on an open disk $B(z_0,R)$ satisfies $$B\bigl(g(z_0),R|g'(z_0)|/4\bigr)\subset g(B(z_0,R)).
 \label{prelim:quarter}$$

For $z,w\in\mathbb H$ and $F\in\mathcal K$, $$Q_{T_zF}(w)=\frac{Q_F(z\cdot w)}{Q_F(z)},\qquad
 T_w(T_zF)=T_{z\cdot w}F,\qquad A_zA_w=A_{z\cdot w}.
 \label{prelim:composition}$$ Each $A_z$ is bounded on $C(\mathcal K)$, and for fixed $\Phi\in C(\mathcal K)$ the map $z\mapsto A_z\Phi$ is continuous in the supremum norm. For $n\ge0$, put $v_n=2^{-n}$ and $u_{n,j}=-1+(2j+1)v_n$, $0\le j<2^n$. Then $$L^n=v_n\sum_{j=0}^{2^n-1} A_{u_{n,j}+iv_n},\qquad
 \|L^n\|=\max_{F\in\mathcal K}L^n\mathbf1(F).
 \label{prelim:dyadic-grid}$$ The limit $$\rho=\lim_{n\to\infty}\|L^n\|^{1/n}
      =\inf_{n\ge1}\|L^n\|^{1/n}
 \label{prelim:rho}$$ exists and satisfies $1\le\rho\le4$. If $\lambda>\rho$, there is $C_\lambda<\infty$ such that $\|L^n\|\le C_\lambda\lambda^n$ for all $n\ge0$.

Suppose that $\rho>2$, and put $\beta=\log_2\rho>1$. There is a Borel probability measure $P$ on $\mathcal K$ such that, for every $z=x+iy\in\mathbb H$ and every nonnegative Borel function $\Phi:\mathcal K\to[0,\infty]$, $$\mathbb E\!\left[|Q_F(z)|^2\Phi(T_zF)\right]
   =y^{-\beta}\mathbb E\Phi(F),
 \label{eq:weighted-covariance}$$ where $\mathbb E$ denotes expectation with respect to $P$.

Assume $\rho>2$, and let $P$ and $\beta$ be as in Lemma 7. For $z=x+iy\in\mathbb H$, define $$q_F(z)=iy\frac{Q'_F(z)}{Q_F(z)} =-iy\frac{F''(z)}{F'(z)} =a_F(z)+ib_F(z), \label{eq:logarithmic-derivative-variable}$$ where $a_F,b_F$ are real. The variables $q_F(i)$ are bounded on $\mathcal K$, and $$\mathbb Ea_F(i)=-\frac\beta2, \qquad \mathbb Eb_F(i)=0, \qquad \mathbb E|q_F(i)|^2=\frac{\beta(\beta+1)}4. \label{eq:law-moments}$$ They also satisfy $$q_{T_zF}(w)=q_F(z\cdot w),\qquad z,w\in\mathbb H. \label{eq:q-affine-covariance}$$
For $P$-almost every $F\in\mathcal K$, for planar area-almost every $\xi\in\mathbb C$, the set $$\{z\in\mathbb H:V_\xi^F(z)\ge\delta\}$$ is compact in $\mathbb H$ for every $\delta>0$.
The function $I:\mathcal K\to[0,\infty]$ is Borel and satisfies $\mathbb EI(F)\le256\pi$. In particular, $I(F)<\infty$ almost surely.

Let $F\in\mathcal K$ satisfy $I(F)<\infty$. Then $$\frac{y^k}{|F(x+iy)|}\longrightarrow0
       \qquad\text{as }|x|+y\longrightarrow\infty.
 \label{escape:tail}$$ For every compact $K\subset\mathbb C$ and $\epsilon>0$, $F^{-1}(K)\cap\{\Im z\ge\epsilon\}$ is compact in $\mathbb H$, and $$H_{F,K}:=\sup\{\Im z:F(z)\in K\}<\infty,$$ where the supremum of an empty set is assigned zero. Moreover, there is $C_{F,K}<\infty$ such that $$\int_{\mathbb R}\mathbf1_K(F(x+i\epsilon))\,dx
       \le C_{F,K}\qquad(\epsilon>0).
 \label{escape:trace}$$
The set of pairs $(F,\xi)\in\mathcal K\times\mathbb C$ for which every closed positive superlevel of $V_\xi^F$ is compact in $\mathbb H$ is Borel.

For every $F\in\mathcal K$ and $z\in\mathbb H$, $$k^2J_F(z)=k(k-1)+(2k-1)a_F(z)+|q_F(z)|^2.
 \label{eq:jacobian-formula}$$ The function $F\mapsto J_F(i)$ is bounded and continuous on $\mathcal K$, and $$k^2\mathbb EJ_F(i)=k(k-1)>0.
 \label{eq:positive-jacobian-mean}$$

Fix $F\in\mathcal K$ and $\xi\in\mathbb C$. Away from the unique possible pole of $V^F_\xi$, put $\ell=\log V^F_\xi$. Then $$\Delta\ell=-\frac{k}{y^2},
 \label{eq:negative-laplacian}$$ and its critical points are exactly the solutions of $G_F(z)=\xi$. At such a point, $$\begin{aligned}
 V^F_\xi(z)&=k y^{k-1}|Q_F(z)|,
 \label{eq:critical-height}\\
 \operatorname{Hess}\ell(z)
 &=\frac{k}{y^2}
 \begin{pmatrix}
  -(k+a_F(z))&b_F(z)\\
  b_F(z)&k-1+a_F(z)
 \end{pmatrix},
 \label{eq:critical-hessian}\\
 \det\operatorname{Hess}\ell(z)&=-\frac{k^4}{y^4}J_F(z).
 \label{eq:critical-hessian-det}
\end{aligned}$$ Consequently a solution with $J_F(z)>0$ is a nondegenerate saddle, and one with $J_F(z)<0$ is a nondegenerate maximum.

The set $\mathcal G$ is Borel. For $P$-almost every $F$, its section $\{\xi:(F,\xi)\in\mathcal G\}$ has full planar area measure.*




*For every $F\in\mathcal K$, $\xi\in\mathbb C$, $t=x_0+iy_0\in\mathbb H$, and $w\in\mathbb H$, set $\widetilde\xi=(\xi-F(t))/(y_0F'(t))$. Then $$\begin{aligned}
 G_{T_tF}(w)&=\frac{G_F(t\cdot w)-F(t)}{y_0F'(t)},
 \label{eq:critical-map-covariance}\\
 q_{T_tF}(w)&=q_F(t\cdot w),\qquad J_{T_tF}(w)=J_F(t\cdot w),
 \label{eq:jacobian-covariance}\\
 V^{T_tF}_{\widetilde\xi}(w)
 &=y_0^{1-k}|F'(t)|V^F_\xi(t\cdot w).
 \label{eq:critical-height-covariance}
\end{aligned}$$ In particular, $(F,\xi)\in\mathcal G$ if and only if $(T_tF,\widetilde\xi)\in\mathcal G$.

Fix a good pair $(F,\xi)$. There are only finitely many critical points of $V^F_\xi$ with value at least $h$, for every $h>0$. For every such $h$, $$\#\{\text{maxima with }V^F_\xi\ge h\}
 \ \ge\
 \#\{\text{saddles with }V^F_\xi\ge h\}.
 \label{eq:cumulative-critical-count}$$ The possible pole is excluded from the maximum count.

Let $$\mathcal D=\{(F,z)\in\mathcal K\times\mathbb H:
                  J_F(z)>0,\ (F,G_F(z))\in\mathcal G\}.$$ There is a Borel map $R:\mathcal D\to\mathbb H$, written $R_F(z)=R(F,z)$, such that, for every $(F,z)\in\mathcal D$, with $z'=R_F(z)$ and $\xi=G_F(z)$, $$G_F(z')=\xi,\qquad J_F(z')<0,\qquad
 V^F_\xi(z')\ge V^F_\xi(z).
 \label{eq:pairing-guarantees}$$ For each fixed $F$, the map $R_F$ is injective on its domain. It is affine equivariant: if $t\in\mathbb H$ and $(F,t\cdot w)\in\mathcal D$, then $$(T_tF,w)\in\mathcal D,\qquad
 R_{T_tF}(w)=t^{\#}\cdot R_F(t\cdot w).
 \label{eq:pairing-covariance}$$
The dyadic transfer operator satisfies $\rho\leq2$.
For every $f\in\mathcal S$ and $0<t<2/3$, $$\int_{\mathbb D}|f'(z)|^t\,dA(z)<\infty.$$

Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb C$ be a simply connected domain whose boundary in the Riemann sphere has at least two points, and let $\varphi:\Omega\to\mathbb D$ be a conformal bijection. For $2<p<\infty$ and $4/3<s<4$, put $q=ps/(p+s-2)$. Then pullback $\varphi^*u=u\circ\varphi$ is bounded from $L_p^1(\mathbb D)$ to $L_q^1(\Omega)$. It is also bounded from $L_\infty^1(\mathbb D)$ to $L_s^1(\Omega)$ for every $4/3<s<4$. The finite bounds on gradient seminorms may depend on the map and the exponents.
